summary: Replaced the per-file literal-scan character allocation with one bounded ArrayPool<char> lease per sequential Search source run. The lease has deterministic ownership and return semantics, short/partial reads remain correct, and emitted SearchMatch rows retain only owned strings and scalar coordinates.

review.reviewer: separate grill-code review pass (no independent subagent was available)

startingState.worktree: Tracked files were clean at scope start; the local ignored campaign state recorded W05-S01 as in_progress. W05-S01 implementation, tests and evidence were added afterward.
startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes the retained pre-existing campaign-state commit; 25 preceding reachable commits carry completed Search scope trailers.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning Search implementation, its tests and W05-S01 evidence were changed. No sibling repository, query-engine adapter, public source signature, release, publish or install surface was modified.
implementation.bufferOwnership: SearchCharBuffer rents one ArrayPool<char> array at the source-scan boundary, passes only the fixed 8,192-character window to TextReader.Read, returns the array exactly once through IDisposable, and tolerates repeated Dispose calls.
implementation.readSemantics: The existing scanner processes only the count returned by each TextReader.Read, preserving irregular short reads, partial final blocks and EOF behavior without inspecting stale pooled characters.
implementation.rowOwnership: SearchMatch rows retain immutable path/literal strings and scalar MatchSpan coordinates; no row stores the pooled array or a borrowed character span.
implementation.cancellation: Cancellation is checked before and after each read and while consuming each returned character; interrupted reads still dispose the reader before the pooled lease is returned.

requiredCoverage: bounded pooled buffer length and deterministic repeated disposal
tiny/irregular short reads and partial final block

gateResults.evidence: The exact owning-repository Release suite exited 0 with 21 projects, 1,363 discovered, 1,329 passed, 0 failed and 34 skips; the focused Search suite exited 0 with 76 passed and 3 platform-conditional skips.

The separate ownership review approved the bounded lease and row-lifetime design; exact source/artifact hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained and verified after commit finalization.
Focused real-reader fixtures prove short reads, partial final input, premature EOF, interrupted reads, deterministic pool return and row values retained after buffer reuse.
The scanner keeps cancellation checks around reads and character consumption, disposes readers before the pooled lease returns, and preserves the existing typed diagnostic boundary.

knownLimitations: The shared .NET pool is exercised and its lease is audited locally; this scope does not claim a process-wide pool performance benchmark.
Readers that violate the .NET TextReader contract by returning an out-of-range count remain outside the source contract.
The repository-wide suite retains 31 existing classified skips and the three W04-S04 platform-conditional symlink fixture skips; no package was published.
